Jurisdictions.kind_authentication_text: You show the record is what it claims to be and that the system kept it intact.
Jurisdictions.kind_authentication_answer: The report is hashed against the commitment, so any change shows.
Jurisdictions.kind_presumption_text: The system is presumed to have worked unless someone challenges it.

ReportedPattern.title: What may have happened
ReportedPattern.note: These are claimants’ own accounts, counted. They are not a finding of fraud: a court decides that.
ReportedPattern.investment_platform: put money into an investment platform or scheme and could not withdraw
ReportedPattern.rug_pull: bought a token or NFT and the team disappeared
ReportedPattern.exchange_service: lost access to funds held by an exchange or wallet service
ReportedPattern.impersonation: sent crypto to someone who presented themselves as someone else
ReportedPattern.recovery_scam: paid a fund-recovery service and got nothing back
ReportedPattern.address_poisoning: sent money to a lookalike of an address they use
ReportedPattern.honeypot_token: bought a token they could not sell
ReportedPattern.extortion: were threatened and asked for crypto
ReportedPattern.fake_job: deposited crypto for work that never paid
ReportedPattern.account_takeover: had someone take over their account
ReportedPattern.romance_scam: were asked for money by someone they had met online
ReportedPattern.phishing: lost money after using a fake website, link or message
ReportedPattern.hack_exploit: lost money when a service, app or contract they used was hacked
ReportedPattern.other: lost money in a way that fits none of the listed kinds

ClaimPage.pay_label: Where did the money come from?
ClaimPage.pay_p2p: By buying crypto from a person (peer to peer)
ClaimPage.wallet_type_label: What kind of wallet is it? (optional)
ClaimPage.funding_tx_hint: The first payment that put money in this wallet, from an exchange or another wallet. It lets us trace where the money came from.
ClaimPage.wallet_browser_extension: Browser extension (such as MetaMask or Phantom)
ClaimPage.wallet_mobile_app: Mobile app (such as Trust Wallet or Coinbase Wallet)
ClaimPage.wallet_hardware: Hardware wallet (such as Ledger or Trezor)
ClaimPage.chain_payment_label: Which chain was the payment on?
ClaimPage.tx_hint: The ID of the payment that sent the money. Your exchange, the ATM receipt or your wallet history shows it. It lets us find where the money went.
ClaimPage.error_tx: This transaction hash does not look right for this chain.
ClaimPage.q_who: Who do you think was behind it?
ClaimPage.unknown_operator: I don’t know who it was
ClaimPage.operator_name: Name of the platform, project or person
ClaimPage.contact_social_dating: A dating app or social media
ClaimPage.contact_messaging: A Telegram or WhatsApp group or message
ClaimPage.contact_referral: A friend or someone I know
ClaimPage.contact_search: A search result or a site I found
ClaimPage.amount_label: About how much did you lose?
ClaimPage.amount_hint: For example 2,500 USDT. We work out the real figure from the chain.
ClaimPage.others_unnamed: {count, plural, =0 {No one else has reported a matching payment yet.} one {1 other person has reported something that matches.} other {# other people have reported something that matches.}}
ClaimPage.hint_investment_platform: What returns were you promised, and by whom? How did you hear about it? What did you pay, and when? When did withdrawals stop, and were you asked for a fee or tax to release your money?
ClaimPage.hint_rug_pull: What was the project, and who promoted it and where? What did you buy and when? What happened to the token and to the team afterwards?
ClaimPage.hint_exchange_service: What service was it and what did you hold there? When did withdrawals stop? What were you told, and what have you tried since?
ClaimPage.hint_impersonation: Who did they say they were, and how did they contact you? What did they ask you to do, and when did you realise? Did they use the same story with others you know of?
ClaimPage.hint_recovery_scam: Who offered to recover your money and how did they find you? What did you pay them, and what did they do or say afterwards? What was the loss they promised to recover?
ClaimPage.hint_wallet_drained: How do you think it happened (a link, an app, a message)? When did you notice? What did you do just before it? Which tokens left, and where did they go?
ClaimPage.hint_address_poisoning: Which address did you mean to pay, and which one did the money go to? Where did you copy it from? When did you notice, and how much was sent?
ClaimPage.hint_honeypot_token: What token was it, and where did you buy it? When did you find you could not sell? Was a fee charged on selling, and who promoted it?
ClaimPage.hint_extortion: How did they contact you, and what did they threaten? What did they ask for, and how much did you send? Have they asked again?
ClaimPage.hint_fake_job: How was the job or task offered? What were you asked to pay or deposit, and what were you promised? When did payments stop?
ClaimPage.hint_account_takeover: Which account was it, and when did you lose access? Did you lose phone service or get odd messages first? What left the account, and where did it go?
ClaimPage.hint_other: What happened, who was involved, what you paid and when, and what has happened since.
ClaimPage.own_lead: Add as many as you like. Never share your seed phrase.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_text: Your wallet will open and ask you to sign the message below. Check that the account is the one on your claim, then approve. It costs nothing.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_none: We can’t see a wallet in this browser. Open this page in your wallet’s browser, or sign by hand.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_wrong_wallet: Your wallet is connected with a different account. Switch to {address} and try again.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_rejected: You declined in your wallet, so nothing was signed.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_failed: Your wallet could not sign. You can sign by hand instead.
ClaimPage.own_wallet_signature: That signature does not match this wallet and message.
ClaimPage.own_hand_copy_text: This is exactly what you will sign. It names your wallet and has a one-time code, so it can’t be reused for another claim.
ClaimPage.own_hand_sign_title: Sign it and paste the signature
ClaimPage.own_hand_sign_text: In your wallet, sign the message as plain text, not as a transaction. Then paste the signature here.
ClaimPage.own_tool_etherscan: One tool signs on every Ethereum-style chain, so Etherscan works for this wallet.
ClaimPage.own_tool_tronscan: On Tronscan, open More, then Tools, then Sign & Verify.
ClaimPage.own_tool_none: There is no signing site for this chain. Use the sign-message feature in your wallet app.
ClaimPage.own_docs_text: Send anything that shows this wallet is yours. A person at Celia reads it and confirms the wallet.
ClaimPage.own_docs_example_app: A screenshot of your wallet app showing this address
ClaimPage.own_docs_example_receipt: A receipt or statement from the exchange or app the money was sent from
ClaimPage.own_docs_example_history: Your wallet’s transaction history for this address, as a screenshot or PDF
ClaimPage.own_docs_safe: Cover anything private. Never include a seed phrase or private key.
ClaimPage.own_docs_files_label: Files: PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF, up to {size} MB each, {count} at a time
ClaimPage.own_err_files_type: Only PNG, JPEG, WebP or PDF files.
ClaimPage.own_err_files_size: Each file must be 4 MB or smaller.
ClaimPage.own_err_files_count: No more than 3 files at a time, and 6 for a claim.
ClaimPage.own_declined: We could not confirm the wallet yet: {note}
ClaimPage.own_video_text: Make a short video, put it online and drop the link here. We review it for what it shows about your case and your wallet. Two to five minutes is plenty.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_who: Say your name, today’s date and the name of the platform.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_wallet: Show your wallet app with this address on screen.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_tx: Open the transaction where your money left and show that it matches your claim.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_sign: If you can, sign the message from the last step, or send a tiny transaction, while recording.
ClaimPage.own_video_show_story: Explain what you were promised, what you paid and what happened.
ClaimPage.own_video_safe: Never show or read out your seed phrase or private key. Cover any balances or details you want to keep private.
ClaimPage.own_video_where: Record with your phone or computer, then upload it to Loom, YouTube (set to unlisted) or Google Drive and copy the share link. Anyone with the link must be able to watch it.
ClaimPage.own_video_link_error: Enter a link that starts with https://
ClaimPage.own_video_quality: We strongly recommend the best quality you can manage: record at the highest resolution, keep the wallet address and the transaction readable on screen, and speak clearly with good light and sound. A clear video is much easier to rely on.
ClaimPage.own_tool_bitcoin: Wallets such as Sparrow, Electrum, Ledger Live and Trezor Suite can sign a message. Use a regular address, not a Taproot one (starting bc1p).
ClaimPage.own_sec_sign_text: Shows you hold the wallet now. Checked straight away.
ClaimPage.own_sign_unsupported: We can’t check signatures on this chain yet.
ClaimPage.own_sec_video_text: Record your screen and drop the link.
ClaimPage.own_withdraw_hint: Deletes your files and the link. A video stays where you uploaded it, so delete it there too.
ClaimPage.own_record_hint: A dated page of what you added, with a fingerprint of each file. Print it or share it.
